events.title: Guido van Rossum steps down as Python BDFL
events.summary: Guido van Rossum stepped down as [Python]'s Benevolent Dictator For Life on July 12, 2018 — ending his central governance role.
events.about: Van Rossum created [Python] in 1991 and guided it through 2/3 migration and community growth. His resignation pushed [Python] toward a formal steering council governance model.

narrative.whyChosen: The BDFL step-down changed how one of the world's largest languages is governed.
narrative.whyImportant: It forced [Python] to institutionalize decision-making beyond a single founder.
narrative.problemSolved: Burnout and mailing-list conflicts showed BDFL model does not scale forever.

events.title: BlackBerry Key2 released
events.summary: BlackBerry released the BlackBerry Key2 — [Android]-powered QWERTY phone from TCL — final BB keyboard flagship.
events.about: BlackBerry dominated enterprise mobile before [iPhone] and [Android]. [Android]-powered qwerty phone from tcl — final bb keyboard flagship. BES-connected apps and push email defined mobile workflows for years.

narrative.whyChosen: The BlackBerry Key2 was a key BlackBerry hardware milestone.
narrative.whyImportant: BlackBerry hardware set expectations for mobile email and messaging security.
narrative.problemSolved: Business users needed secure mobile email before modern smartphone platforms.

events.title: Apache Kafka 2.0 released
events.summary: The Apache [Kafka] project released version 2.0 on July 28, 2018 — adding OAuth2 authentication, prefixed ACLs, and improved [Kafka] Streams windowed aggregations.
events.about: [Kafka] 2.0 matured the event-streaming platform [microservices] rely on — producers, consumers, and [Kafka] Streams for real-time pipelines. It cemented [Kafka] as the default log backbone between services.

narrative.whyChosen: [Kafka] 2.0 marked the platform's transition to enterprise-grade streaming infrastructure.
narrative.whyImportant: It expanded [Kafka] beyond a message queue into a full event streaming system.
narrative.problemSolved: [Teams] needed durable, replayable event logs between distributed services.
